text: Welcome to Microsoft Power Automate, the first course in Business Process Automation. Throughout this course you'll build real flows for Castlebridge Logistics, a fictional regional trucking and warehousing company. Before you touch the designer, this lesson answers the question everything else depends on: what is Power Automate, and where does it fit?

Power Automate is Microsoft's low-code automation service, and the name actually covers three capabilities. Cloud flows connect apps you already use, like SharePoint, Outlook, and Teams. Desktop flows handle robotic process automation for older applications that have no modern connector. And process mining studies your existing system logs to find where a process is actually slow, before you automate anything.

Every flow starts from the same home page. The left navigation pane gets you to My flows and Approvals, the search bar finds templates and connectors fast, and the environment switcher confirms which Castlebridge environment you're building in. This is the screen you'll open to start nearly everything in this course.

Castlebridge Logistics automates with this tool for a simple reason: it connects apps the staff already use daily, without waiting on a developer. A dispatch supervisor can own her own shipping approval flow end to end. And it scales from one person's instant flow up to automation running across the whole warehouse operation.
Hold onto that shape — cloud flows, desktop flows, and process mining, all under one name. Up next, Lesson 2: the two building blocks every flow is made of, triggers and actions.
